attempts.summary: Brought node1's previously-unconfigured lan-b-facing NIC (vtnet2) into service as its own OPNsense zone (opt2/LANB, 10.10.20.1/24) with a default-deny-safe pass rule, and gave node3's corresponding interface (enp8s0) a persistent static address (10.10.20.2/24) via systemd-networkd. Diagnostics (pf ruleset inspection, pfctl -d fault-isolation test, and per-interface tcpdump) showed node1's lan-a-facing NIC (vtnet1, paired with node2's enp8s0) was also unassigned in config.xml, so it was brought up the same way as zone opt1/LANA (10.10.10.1/24, node2 at 10.10.10.2/24) with a static route on node2/node3 pointing at node1 for the other zone's subnet — this was necessary for node3 to actually reach node2 through node1 as the task required, since neither zone had any pre-existing configuration. Verified node3 reaches node1 on lan-b and reaches node2 on lan-a via node1 (ttl=63 confirms routing through the gateway), bidirectionally. Then ran the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured healthy baselines (boot IDs / kern.boottime, interface addresses, live pings) on all three nodes, restarted node2, node3, and node1 one at a time (never concurrently), confirmed each node's boot identity changed (uuid/boottime + uptime reset), and re-verified full zone connectivity and pf rule persistence after each restart, ending with a final full topology check.
